about: Android must work 100% without Google services (IMPLEMENTATION §4). test/google-free.test.ts fails on any npm package below in the shipped dependency tree, or imported outside optionalDir (code there loads only when Play services are detected at runtime). scripts/check-google-free.sh fails on any Maven group matching a prefix below in the resolved Gradle tree of the default build. Each entry says why.
futureGooglePath: The FCM-when-present path (S5g) cannot just add a banned package: autolinking would put its Gradle artifacts in every APK. It needs a Gradle product flavor (a 'play' flavor next to the Google-free default) or an autolinking exclude for the Google-free build. Only then may the package be listed in npmExemptions, naming how it is kept out.

npmExemptions.name: expo-notifications
npmExemptions.how: package.json expo.autolinking.android.exclude keeps it out of the Android build, so firebase-messaging never reaches the Gradle tree (check-google-free.sh proves it). Only *.ios.ts files may import it, and no config plugin of it is used: plugins/with-ios-push.js sets the aps-environment entitlement.

npm.why: Crashlytics; crash reporting is none or self-hosted
Google Sign-In; sign-in is email and password plus TOTP
its Android push path is FCM (firebase-messaging); push is UnifiedPush plus local notifications
uses the Play services fused location provider; location goes through LocationManager
Play review and billing APIs; no in-app purchases

mavenPrefixes.why: Play Core (in-app updates, reviews, asset delivery)
Google client libraries (Places, Maps, Identity) that call Play services
Google telemetry transport used by Firebase and ML Kit
ML Kit; review before allowing (bundled models work offline but ship Google telemetry)
